title: Passive 1 (is done / was done)
subtitle: is done / was done
summary: Use the passive (be + past participle) to say what happens to the subject, especially when who does the action is unknown or unimportant.

left.label: Active: what the subject does
left.text: When we use an active verb, we say what the subject does.
examples: My grandfather was a builder. He **built** this house in 1981.
It's a big company. It **employs** two hundred people.

right.label: Passive: what happens to the subject
right.text: When we use a passive verb, we say what happens to the subject.
examples: 'How old is this house?' 'It **was built** in 1981.'
Two hundred people **are employed** by the company.

lesson.heading: When we use the passive
lesson.text: When we use the passive, who or what causes the action is often unknown or unimportant. If we want to say who does or what causes the action, we use **by**.

examples.text: A lot of money **was stolen** in the robbery.
examples.note: somebody stole it, but we don't know who
does somebody clean it? - it's not important who

examples.text: This house was built **by** my grandfather.
Two hundred people are employed **by** the company.

lesson.heading: The form: be + past participle
lesson.text: The passive is **be** (is/was etc.) + **past participle** (done/cleaned/seen etc.): (be) done, (be) cleaned, (be) damaged, (be) built, (be) seen. The past participle often ends in -ed (cleaned/damaged etc.), but many important verbs are irregular (built/done/stolen etc.).

lesson.heading: Present simple and past simple
rows: Somebody cleans this room every day. (clean(s) / see(s) etc.)
This room is cleaned every day. (am/is/are + cleaned/seen etc.)
Somebody cleaned this room yesterday. (cleaned/saw etc.)
This room was cleaned yesterday. (was/were + cleaned/seen etc.)

lesson.heading: Present simple passive
lesson.text: **am/is/are + past participle**. Questions put am/is/are before the subject.

examples.text: Many accidents **are caused** by careless driving.
**I'm not invited** to parties very often.

lesson.heading: Past simple passive
lesson.text: **was/were + past participle**. Questions put was/were before the subject.

examples.text: We **were woken up** by a loud noise during the night.
'Did you go to the party?' 'No, **I wasn't invited**.'
How much money **was stolen** in the robbery?

lesson.text: Ask: does the subject do the action (active) or does something happen to the subject (passive)? The camera was stolen - the camera didn't do anything.

exercises.explanation: Something happened to the house in the past, so use the past simple passive: was built.
A general fact about what happens to cheese: present simple passive (is made).

exercises.prompt: The roof of the building ___ in a storm a few days ago.
exercises.explanation: A few days ago is past, and something happened to the roof: was damaged.

exercises.prompt: Is the verb in each sentence active or passive?

items.text: While I was on holiday, my camera was stolen from my hotel room.
While I was on holiday, my camera disappeared from my hotel room.
Robert's parents died when he was very young.
Robert and his sister were brought up by their grandparents.
The boat hit a rock and sank quickly.
Bill was fired from his job. He wasn't very good at it.
Sue resigned from her job because she didn't enjoy it any more.

exercises.prompt: You ___ to the party. Why didn't you go?
exercises.explanation: Somebody invited you (past), so: you were invited.

exercises.prompt: Water ___ most of the earth's surface.
exercises.explanation: Water does the covering, so the verb is active: covers. Compare: the surface is covered by water.
Present simple passive question: What + is + subject + past participle, with the preposition at the end.

exercises.statement: Many accidents are caused by careless driving.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Present simple passive (are caused), with by to say what causes the accidents.

exercises.statement: There was an accident last night, but fortunately nobody injured.
exercises.explanation: Fortunately nobody was injured. Something happened to the people, so we need the passive: was injured.

exercises.prompt: It can be noisy living here, but I ___ by it.
exercises.explanation: The noise bothers me, so I am (not) bothered by it - present simple passive with the full past participle.

exercises.prompt: People warned us not to go out alone. Write a passive sentence beginning We ...
exercises.answer: We were warned not to go out alone.
exercises.explanation: Past simple passive: were + warned. Who warned us is not important.

exercises.prompt: I haven't seen these flowers before. What ___?
exercises.explanation: The flowers don't do the calling, so use the passive question: What are they called?
